answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to forge a costly, verifiable work history before it can trade: like a wharf that only admits ships with a logged cargo record, the network admits agents only after they complete paid, attested tasks over time. A newcomer starts with tiny limits and earns trust gradually, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means paying real compute and fees for each one, while an opal-grade reputation token, earned slowly and lost instantly on fraud, makes the attack uneconomical.
